Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To compare several items across the same few attributes: tokens and their values, people and their roles, results and their counts.
  • As the accessible data-table alternative next to a chart, with the same numbers.

When not to use

  • For a list where each item has one name and a detail or two: use cmp-list-row.
  • For layout. Never use a table to place things side by side.
  • For more columns than fit on a phone without scrolling; reduce the columns or show a list on narrow screens.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • default — comfortable rows with hairline dividers and a muted header row. The base class alone; no modifier class.
  • compact — tighter rows and smaller text, for dense reference data and chart alternatives.

Anatomy

  • Root: <table class="ds-table"> (add ds-table--compact), a real HTML table.
  • Caption: <caption class="ds-table__caption"> first, naming what the table shows. Always present; hide it with ds-visually-hidden only when a visible heading right above already says the same.
  • Header: <thead> with <th scope="col"> cells; a first column that names each row uses <th scope="row">.
  • Body: <tbody> with <td> cells.
  • Numeric cells: add ds-table__numeric to the th and td of a number column, so numbers align on the right and line up digit by digit.

Accessibility

  • A native table with a caption and scoped header cells, so screen readers announce each value with its row and column.
  • Header text uses text-muted on the page surface, and cells text-default, both AA in every theme.
  • Never encode a value by colour alone in a cell; write the value (a status pill is fine, because it carries a word).
  • Wide tables scroll inside the area that holds them, never the whole page.

Interaction

  • Not interactive by default; rows do not highlight on hover, so nothing suggests a click that does nothing (int-04).
  • When a cell holds a link or control, that element carries the focus ring (int-02).

Content rules

  • Column headings are short nouns in sentence case: "Token", "Light", "Used by".
  • Put the identifying column first, then the values people compare, then notes.
  • Numbers use the same unit and precision down a column, with the unit in the heading: "Size (px)".
  • Empty cells show an en dash (–), never blank.

Do and don't

  • Do sort rows in the order people look for them, and say the order in the caption when it matters.
  • Do keep tables inside a flush card or a sunken section when they need a frame.
  • Don't zebra-stripe rows or draw vertical rules; hairlines between rows are enough.
  • Don't truncate values with an ellipsis; wrap them.
